baseline.policy: Every write-capable database call from a named HTTP, AI, or operational delivery source is an entry. Query-only persistence access remains allowed. A baseline edit is documented only when this file and its SHA-256 lock change together and the entry names its owning migration ticket.

invariants: The nudge timestamp belongs to the authenticated Habit owner
Dismissing a nudge must not change Habit lifecycle state or streak facts
entries.atomicity: Single Habit-row update; no cross-record transaction is required by the current operation.

invariants: Defaults are scoped to the authenticated user and source type
The user/source uniqueness rule prevents duplicate default intent
Default channels and relative timing remain valid Reminder Configuration
entries.atomicity: One database upsert protected by the user/source uniqueness constraint; no source lifecycle transaction currently owns it.

entries.operation: Remove an exercise from a routine
invariants: The routine exercise must belong to a user-owned routine
Removing an exercise must preserve the remaining routine order and targets
entries.atomicity: Single routine_exercises delete; ownership and routine-level policy remain in the generic persistence adapter.

invariants: Target values must match the exercise's supported fields
The routine exercise remains attached to its user-owned routine
Sort order and target defaults remain stable
entries.atomicity: Single routine_exercises update; no routine/workout mutation authority currently owns the aggregate.

entries.operation: Add an exercise to a routine
invariants: The exercise must be valid and the routine must be user-owned
The next sort order must preserve deterministic routine ordering
Target and rest defaults must be applied consistently
entries.atomicity: A max-sort-order read followed by an insert is not atomic at the delivery boundary and can race under concurrent edits.

invariants: The routine must be user-owned
Dependent routine exercises must not survive the routine deletion
entries.atomicity: One routine-row delete relies on database cascade cleanup; the routine authoring behavior is not a shared domain authority.

invariants: The routine must be user-owned
Name and notes normalization must be consistent with routine-to-workout conversion
entries.atomicity: Single routine-row update; no shared routine aggregate or conversion authority currently owns the operation.

invariants: The routine is owned by the authenticated user
Routine identity and defaults remain compatible with routine-to-workout conversion
entries.atomicity: Single routine-row insert; subsequent routine-exercise writes are separate and not part of this delivery transaction.

priorArt.operation: Reminder Delivery snooze, completion, retry retirement, and unsupported-source retirement
invariants: User transitions are scoped to the explicit authenticated identity
Only trusted operational dispatch may record failure, stale, or unsupported-source outcomes
Expected delivery state makes retries idempotent and concurrent attempts conflicted
Reminder Configuration timing and channels remain owned by source lifecycle authorities
priorArt.atomicity: ReminderDelivery makes the storage-independent decision and SupabaseReminderDeliveryPersistence commits one expected-state transition through transition_reminder_delivery.
priorArt.evidence: HTTP reminders, AI dismissal/snooze, and cron completion all call createReminderDelivery; the delivery adapter rejects channels and configuration-shaped transition requests.

priorArt.operation: Task creation, editing, ordering, completion, and status intent
invariants: Task defaults, ownership, status synchronization, ordering, and recurring delegation
priorArt.atomicity: Task Writes uses narrow persistence capabilities and transactional recurring lifecycle boundaries where required.
priorArt.evidence: HTTP task routes and lib/ai/tools/tasks.ts call createTaskWrites; no qualifying TasksDB write call remains in delivery sources.

invariants: Ownership-safe not-found outcomes, recurring scopes, completed-history preservation, and regeneration prevention
priorArt.atomicity: Recurring deletion scopes commit task, occurrence, and series effects through one database transaction boundary.
priorArt.evidence: app/api/tasks/[id]/route.ts, app/api/recurring-tasks/[id]/route.ts, and lib/ai/tools/tasks.ts route deletion through Task Writes.

priorArt.operation: Recurring Task Series creation, revision, coverage, pause/resume, ending, and occurrence actions
invariants: Series identity, Series Revision effective dates, Coverage Horizon, occurrence lineage, and lifecycle state
priorArt.atomicity: Series mutations use lifecycle transaction boundaries; reads may use focused query adapters after coverage is ensured.
priorArt.authority: lib/recurring-tasks/lifecycle.ts, its Supabase adapters, and the declared compatibility adapter
priorArt.evidence: Recurring-task routes, the calendar feed, the dashboard/read path, the optional prewarm job, and AI tools call lifecycle and Series/Occurrence adapters; ordinary task queries remain task-model queries, direct recurring persistence writes and legacy projection writers are absent, and the post-cutover storage/rollback/RLS proof is in docs/architecture/recurring-task-lifecycle-contract.md and the registered SQL fixtures.

invariants: Habit log, streak, schedule, milestone deduplication, and non-critical reaction policy
priorArt.atomicity: Habit Completion coordinates the core log and streak state through its persistence boundary; milestone reactions are post-commit policy.

priorArt.operation: Habit creation, editing, pause/resume, graduation, reactivation, and deletion
invariants: Habit ownership, lifecycle state transitions, frequency normalization, limits, history, and dependent cleanup
priorArt.atomicity: Habit Writes uses narrow persistence ports and atomic database functions for lifecycle transitions that coordinate history.
priorArt.evidence: Habit HTTP routes and lib/ai/tools/habits.ts call createHabitWrites; the remaining nudge endpoint is separately inventoried.

priorArt.operation: Workout start, active editing, completion, and discard
invariants: One active session, ownership, exercise/set ordering, supported fields, terminal status, and derived duration
priorArt.atomicity: Workout Writes delegates coordinated workout, exercise, and set changes to atomic RPC boundaries where required.
priorArt.evidence: Workout HTTP routes and lib/ai/tools/workouts.ts call createWorkoutWrites; no qualifying WorkoutsDB write call remains in delivery sources.

invariants: Exercise order, target mapping, supported set types, ownership, and no partial conversion
priorArt.atomicity: The conversion store owns the multi-row routine/workout transaction boundary.
priorArt.evidence: app/api/routines/[id]/start/route.ts and app/api/workouts/[id]/save-as-routine/route.ts use shared conversion authorities.

invariants: Entry ownership, date uniqueness, link target ownership, and dependent-link cleanup
priorArt.atomicity: Journal Writes owns the required entry/link transaction boundaries.
priorArt.evidence: Journal HTTP routes and lib/ai/tools/journal.ts call createJournalWrites; JournalEntriesDB use in delivery remains query-only.

invariants: Project ownership, normalization, status transitions, sort order, and dependent Task unassignment
priorArt.atomicity: Project Writes owns project and dependent-task changes through the persistence boundary.
priorArt.evidence: Project HTTP routes and lib/ai/tools/projects.ts call createProjectWrites; ProjectsDB writes are absent from delivery sources.

priorArt.operation: Calendar event create, update, delete, and linked calendar Reminder Configuration
invariants: Event ownership, recurrence, linked reminder reconciliation, and no orphaned Reminder Configuration
priorArt.atomicity: Scheduling Lifecycle commits event and linked reminder changes as one lifecycle operation.
priorArt.evidence: Calendar HTTP and AI adapters call SchedulingLifecycle for update/delete and use its write boundary for linked reminders.

invariants: Event normalization, recurrence, category ownership, and linked Reminder Configuration creation
priorArt.atomicity: Scheduling Writes delegates event-plus-reminder creation to the Scheduling persistence transaction boundary.
priorArt.evidence: app/api/calendar-events/route.ts and lib/ai/tools/calendar.ts call createSchedulingWrites for creation.

priorArt.operation: Task Reminder Configuration create, replace, and removal
invariants: Task ownership, relative/absolute timing, channel normalization, and source-lifecycle consistency
priorArt.atomicity: Task Writes commits the task-owned Reminder Configuration through its database function boundary.
priorArt.evidence: Task reminder HTTP and AI adapters call createTaskWrites(...).configureReminders; generic task reminder writes are absent.

priorArt.operation: Habit Reminder Configuration create, replace, and removal
invariants: Habit ownership and no-disclosure outcomes, normalized timing and channel intent, source isolation, and terminal delivery-history preservation
priorArt.atomicity: Habit Writes commits the complete Habit-owned Reminder Configuration through the configure_habit_reminders database function; source deletion cleanup remains in the Habit lifecycle transaction.
priorArt.evidence: HTTP and AI Habit reminder adapters call createHabitWrites(...).configureReminders; generic Habit Reminder Configuration writes are absent from delivery sources.

excluded.reason: These delivery sources have only direct query access for ownership checks or projections; any lifecycle side effects use an already-migrated authority, and the scanner does not classify get/list/select access as a write bypass.
These writes belong to categories, exercise catalog, push-subscription, or profile-preference ownership and are outside the eight-domain migration inventory.
